newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Banco Itau moves into Brazil insurance.
newsitem.headline: Banco Itau moves into Brazil insurance.

text.p: Brazil's Banco Itau SA will take control of its sister company, Itau Seguros, as part of a strategy to strengthen its position in the country's booming insurance market, the bank's president said on Tuesday.
Banco Itau, the country's second-largest private bank, will acquire 91.6 percent of the insurer from their holding company, Itausa, under a proposed restructuring of the group's insurance interests.

"We understood that the restructuring would create better conditions for Itau's development in the insurance sector," said Roberto Setubal, president of Banco Itau, which already controls Itau Previdencia e Seguros, a pension plan, and Itau Capitalizacao, a capitalization firm.
To allow the transfer of control, Itau Seguros will split into two units -- one composed of the insurer's holdings in other operations of the group and a second comprising the insurance operations.
Banco Itau will control the latter under the proposal, which is to be submitted to shareholders meeting on April 28.

Itau Seguros has a 13.48 percent stake in Banco Itau and a 14.42 percent stake in Duratex SA, a building supply company. Those stakes are to be grouped under a sub-holding that will remain under Itausa's control, Setubal said.
At a news conference, Setubal said Itau Seguros would have total capital of about 500 million reais after a capital increase of 200 million reais.

Itau's president said he could not forecast the precise impact of the takeover on the bank's results, though he said he expected the insurer would boost the bank's earnings. He said much depended on the growth of the insurance industry in coming years.
The Brazilian insurance industry is expected to grow 15 percent a year by 2,000, analysts say.

Most of optimism for future growth of Brazil's insurance sector reflects the success of the country's anti-inflation program, which has increased purchasing power, allowed Brazilians to save money and make long-term investments.
Itau will continue focusing on life, car insurance and pension plans, Setubal said. He said he expected its pension plan business to grow by more than 100 percent in 1997.

Itau Seguros ranked as the third-largest insurance company in Brazil last year, with a 8.6 percent market share, said Luiz de Campos Salles, the insurer's president. It also ranked the third in car insurance, with 600,000 policies.
The company ended the year with total premiums of 974.7 million reais.
